homonyms.basis: The census row carries no disambiguation field. No card is a homonym, and T composes no other entity under the name. 'BANNEDTHOUGHT.NET' is the census's other name for the entity (aka) and the site's own capitalisation; 'Banned Thought' has no Wikipedia title (B4). The distinct entities below are named by the field or the census beside the entity and are never senses of its name.
distinct_entities: the parties whose documents it holds: the Communist Party of India (Maoist); the CPN (Revolutionary Maoist) and the CPN (Maoist Centre), the two Nepali parties it files side by side; the CPI(M-L) parties; the Communist Party of the Philippines (B1 F10–F12; B2 F29, F30)
the international associations it holds: CCOMPOSA, RIM, the ICL, the Comintern (B1 F15)
the YUMPU account named bannedthought.net, a third-party platform's page of copies, its maker unstated (B3 F32)
J.R. Valila and the Social Sciences and Development Review, the citing article and its journal (B2 F26)
the Marxists Internet Archive, the second holder card 2 cites (B2 F31); a census neighbour, row marxists-internet-archive, built in parallel
the Indian government Internet censorship agency, whose letter the site posts (B1 F8)

captures.description: THE SITE, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-31: '[BannedThought.net] is an online digital archive that collects, preserves, and publishes censored documents, periodicals, and writings related to international communist movements, Maoist theory, and revolutionary left-wing struggles worldwide.' Purpose; content scope (CPP, CPI (Maoist)); censorship status. Three cards: the site, Philippine E-Journals, YUMPU.

atoms.evidence: BANNEDTHOUGHT.NET - Struggling against the suppression of progressive ideas.

is an online digital archive that collects, preserves, and publishes censored documents, periodicals, and writings related to international communist movements, Maoist theory, and revolutionary left-wing struggles worldwide.
including materials from the Communist Party of the Philippines (CPP), the Communist Party of India (Maoist), and broader Marxist-Leninist-Maoist movements.
It aims to oppose the suppression of progressive or radical ideas by making rare, out-of-print, and politically censored texts freely accessible.
